traffic.title: Player traffic
traffic.desc: Logical request path. HTTP goes through one NLB and NGINX; each pwn challenge has its own NLB straight to the pods.

steps.t: The browser resolves ctf.whitehats-ctf.com. ExternalDNS created that Route 53 record from the CTFd Ingress, and it points at the HTTP NLB.
The browser opens TCP 443 to the NLB. The NLB does not decrypt anything; it forwards the connection to an NGINX pod IP (ip target type).
NGINX terminates TLS with the ctfd-tls certificate (Let's Encrypt, issued by cert-manager) and matches the Host header ctf.whitehats-ctf.com.
NGINX proxies to Service ctfd:8000, which has one pod. One of its 2 gunicorn workers takes the request.
CTFd validates the session and reads cached config from Redis, then reads teams, solves and challenge values from MariaDB to build the page.
POST /api/v1/challenges/attempt reaches NGINX through the same NLB as every other HTTP request.
There is no rate limit on the CTFd Ingress at HEAD. A 100 rps limit was added on 2026-06-26 and removed again in the archive commit.
CTFd writes the submission and, if correct, the solve to MariaDB. Dynamic values (1000 → 100 over 31 solves) are computed from the solve count.
Cached scoreboard entries in Redis are invalidated. The Discord plugin posts the first 3 solves of each challenge (see the Operations view).
{name}.challenges.whitehats-ctf.com resolves to the same HTTP NLB as the scoreboard. ExternalDNS made one record per Ingress host.
Same NLB, same two NGINX pods. Each challenge Ingress has its own Let's Encrypt certificate ({name}-tls).
NGINX applies the challenge limits: 20 requests/s, burst ×1, 15 concurrent connections per client address, else HTTP 503. It then picks one of the 2 pods round-robin, with no stickiness.
The player copies nc k8s-challeng-…elb.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com 7331 from CTFd. builder.py wrote that hostname into connection_info after Pulumi created the NLB.
The challenge's own NLB forwards the TCP connection to one of 3 pod IPs. No NGINX, no TLS, no rate limit.
socat forks a fresh copy of the binary on a PTY for this connection. 60 seconds without traffic and socat closes it.
File links point at ctf.whitehats-ctf.com/files/…, so downloads take the scoreboard path. The Ingress allows request bodies up to 50 MB.
CTFd reads the file from /var/uploads, a 5 GiB gp3 EBS volume mounted ReadWriteOnce. This volume is why CTFd can only run as one pod.

network.title: AWS network
network.desc: Physical layout in ap-southeast-1, drawn the way terravision groups resources: account, region, VPC, availability zone, subnet.

steps.t: Route 53 returns the NLB's addresses. Each NLB has one node, and one public IP, in every AZ it spans.
Traffic enters the VPC through the internet gateway, the only public entry.
The NLB node in one AZ receives the connection. Cross-zone load balancing is off by default for NLBs and nothing turns it on, so each AZ's node forwards to targets in its own AZ.
With ip targets the NLB sends straight to the pod's VPC IP (VPC CNI gives every pod a real subnet address). The source address the pod sees is the NLB's private IP, not the player's.
Nodes sit in private subnets with no public IPs. All outbound traffic from every AZ leaves through the one NAT gateway in ap-southeast-1a.
There are no VPC endpoints, so ECR image pulls and S3 backup uploads also go through that NAT gateway.
EBS volumes live in one AZ. MariaDB, Redis and the two CTFd volumes are bound to whichever AZ their pod first landed in (WaitForFirstConsumer). A rescheduled pod must return to that AZ.

deploy.title: Build and deploy
deploy.desc: What the operator runs, in order, and what each tool creates. Columns run left to right in deploy order.

steps.t: make deploy-eks first restores any wh-2026 secrets stuck in 'pending deletion' (Secrets Manager keeps deleted secrets 7 days), then runs terraform init.
Apply 1 is targeted at the VPC, EKS, the Pulumi state bucket and the scenarios ECR repo. The Kubernetes and Helm providers need a live cluster endpoint before they can plan.

Apply 2 runs the full config: IRSA roles, Helm releases (LB controller, ExternalDNS, ingress-nginx, cert-manager, Cluster Autoscaler), the gp3 StorageClass, alarms and the Lambda. The 2026-06-23 run created 72 resources.
make deploy-ctfd builds the CTFd image from a separate ../../CTFd checkout (CTFd 3.8.5 plus plugins).
The image goes to ECR wh-2026-ctfd:latest. A lifecycle rule keeps the last 5 images.
pulumi up on utils/ctfd creates the namespace, Secrets, PVCs, MariaDB, Redis, CTFd, the Ingress and PodDisruptionBudgets. Backup and healthcheck CronJobs are applied by their own make targets.
make build-images first applies the ECR Terraform and writes registry details into config.ini, then runs builder.py.
For every challenge.yml whose challenge_type is shared-web or shared-tcp, builder.py builds the Dockerfile and pushes it to ECR wh-2026:{name}.
builder.py writes the challenge list (name, image, port, replicas) into the Pulumi stack config and runs pulumi up on web-shared and shared-tcp.
Kubernetes gets one Deployment per challenge, plus an Ingress (web) or a LoadBalancer Service (pwn). The LB controller then creates one NLB per pwn challenge.
builder.py calls ctf challenge install so new challenges exist in CTFd.
ctf challenge sync pushes descriptions, flags, hints, files and scoring from every challenge.yml to the CTFd admin API.
ctfcli doesn't update connection_info for these types. builder.py reads each NLB hostname from the shared-tcp stack outputs and PATCHes connection_info directly.

ops.title: Operations
ops.desc: Monitoring, alerting, backups, certificates, DNS and node scaling. Dashed lines were deployed but never shown to work.

steps.t: The amazon-cloudwatch-observability add-on runs the CloudWatch agent and Fluent Bit on every node and ships pod and node metrics to Container Insights.
Five alarms watch those metrics: ingress-nginx running containers < 1, node count below the minimum, MariaDB memory > 80%, node filesystem > 85%, node memory > 85%.
A breached alarm publishes to SNS topic wh-2026-eks-alerts, which emails every address in alarm_notification_emails.
The same topic invokes the sns_to_discord Lambda, which reformats the alarm and posts it to Discord. Alarm history was destroyed with the account, so nobody knows whether any fired.
At minute 0 every hour, a CronJob pod (mariadb:10.11 image) runs mysqldump against the in-cluster mariadb Service.

A second container gzips the dump and uploads it with aws s3 cp, using the ctfd-backup IRSA role. The bucket is versioned, SSE-S3 encrypted, and expires objects after 30 days. The 12:00 UTC event-day dump survives in this repo.
Every 5 minutes healthcheck.py curls each web challenge URL and runs nc -z against each pwn NLB host and port.
Failures go to Discord only if the healthcheck-webhook Secret exists. Nothing in the repo creates it, so unless someone made it by hand, alerts were skipped with a warning in the pod log.
CTFd's Discord plugin posts 'Congratulations to {user} from {team} for the {n} solve on {challenge}' for the first 3 solves (DISCORD_WEBHOOK_LIMIT=3).
An Ingress annotated cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod makes cert-manager open an ACME order for that hostname.
cert-manager proves domain control with DNS-01: it writes an _acme-challenge TXT record to Route 53 using its IRSA role.

Let's Encrypt checks the TXT record, then signs the certificate. cert-manager stores it as a Secret that NGINX serves. Let's Encrypt allows 5 duplicate certificates per week, which matters on repeated rebuilds.

ExternalDNS watches Ingresses and Services and upserts A/ALIAS records for their hosts in whitehats-ctf.com, plus TXT ownership records (owner id wh-2026-eks). policy: sync means it also deletes records it owns once the Ingress is gone.

When a pod is Pending because no node has room for its requests, Cluster Autoscaler raises the node group's desired size, up to the max. A node that stays under 50% requested for 10 minutes is drained and removed.

players.title: Players
players.body: Everyone reaches the platform over the public internet: the browser for the scoreboard and web challenges, nc for pwn challenges. Every player gets the same URL or nc command for a challenge; nothing in the network knows which team a player is on. Teams exist only inside CTFd, for scoring.
facts: 412 users in 142 teams created; 106 teams scored at least one flag
Peak: 1,962 submissions between 10:00 and 11:00 SGT
Registration was open, so 6 automated 'codex' teams also joined

r53.title: Route 53
r53.body: The public hosted zone existed before this stack, and Terraform takes its ID as hosted_zone_id. ExternalDNS writes the records for Ingress hosts; cert-manager writes the short-lived _acme-challenge TXT records.
facts: ctf.whitehats-ctf.com → HTTP NLB
{challenge}.challenges.whitehats-ctf.com → same NLB, one record per Ingress
Pwn NLBs get no friendly name; players see the raw *.elb.amazonaws.com hostname
Route 53 is a global service; it's drawn inside the region only for space

nlbh.title: NLB · HTTP(S)
nlbh.body: The AWS Load Balancer Controller creates this internet-facing Network Load Balancer from the ingress-nginx LoadBalancer Service. It works at layer 4: it passes TCP 80 and 443 through to NGINX pod IPs and never sees HTTP.
facts: Annotations: aws-load-balancer-type nlb, scheme internet-facing, nlb-target-type ip
No proxy protocol and no client-IP preservation are configured, so NGINX likely sees the NLB's private IP as the source
Not in Terraform state; the destroy script deletes it before VPC deletion

nlbt.title: 5 × NLB · TCP
nlbt.body: Each shared-tcp challenge's Service has type LoadBalancer, so the LB controller creates a dedicated internet-facing NLB per challenge. Listener port = challenge port.
facts: loop :7331 · xoph :1337 · library :9001 · postman :1111 · another :9999
ip targets → the 3 pod IPs directly
Hostname is exported from the Pulumi stack and written to CTFd connection_info
Recreating the stack changes every hostname (healthcheck config must then be updated)

nginx.title: NGINX ×2
nginx.body: The single HTTP front door for the cluster. It terminates TLS, routes by Host header to CTFd or a web challenge, and enforces the per-client rate limits set as Ingress annotations.
facts: 2 replicas since 8bcebde (2026-06-27), preferred anti-affinity on kubernetes.io/hostname
--default-ssl-certificate ingress-nginx/wildcard-challenges-tls is the fallback cert
Each NGINX pod keeps its own rate-limit counters
CloudWatch alarm fires if running containers drop below 1

ctfd.title: CTFd ×1
ctfd.body: The scoreboard, API and admin UI. A custom image built from a separate CTFd checkout, with the Discord first-blood plugin. It runs as one pod because its upload and log volumes are ReadWriteOnce EBS disks.
facts: Requests 500m CPU / 512Mi, limit 2 CPU / 2Gi
WORKERS=2, REVERSE_PROXY=true, SECRET_KEY from the ctfd-admin Secret
Recreate strategy and a PDB with maxUnavailable 0: an update means a short outage
An init container chowns the volumes to uid 1001

web.title: Web challenges
web.body: xssive-login :3000, pokemon-portal :3000, inspectpost :80, a-thousand-suns :5000, base64converter :5000. Each has a ClusterIP Service and an Ingress at {name}.challenges.whitehats-ctf.com. Every player shares the same 2 pods.
facts: Requests 100m / 128Mi, limits 500m / 512Mi per pod
Rate limit: 20 rps, burst ×1, 15 connections, 503 on excess
Replicas raised 1 → 2 during the event (committed in the 2026-09-02 archive)
3 of the 5 keep state inside the pod; see section 05

pwn.title: Pwn challenges
pwn.body: Each container runs socat TCP-LISTEN,fork, which starts a new process of the challenge binary for every connection on a PTY. Two connections never share a process, even from teammates, but every player shares the container.
facts: Default 3 replicas (shared_tcp_replicas in config.ini)
socat -T60 closes idle connections after 60 s
No rate limit or connection cap
automountServiceAccountToken: false, so a shell gets no Kubernetes credentials

mariadb.title: MariaDB ×1
mariadb.body: CTFd's database: users, teams, challenges, submissions, solves, awards, config. Runs in the cluster as a Deployment on a 10 GiB gp3 volume, not on RDS.
facts: utf8mb4, wait_timeout 28800
Requests 250m / 512Mi, limit 1 CPU / 1Gi
PDB maxUnavailable 0; Recreate strategy
Alarm when pod memory > 80%

redis.title: Redis ×1
redis.body: CTFd's cache and session store. Kept at one replica on purpose: a second Redis on the same volume caused split-brain and 403 errors from broken sessions.
facts: Requests 100m / 128Mi, limit 500m / 512Mi
Data on a 1 GiB gp3 volume

pvc.title: CTFd volumes
pvc.body: Challenge attachments and CTFd logs on gp3 EBS volumes. ReadWriteOnce means only one node can mount them, which pins CTFd to one pod.
facts: StorageClass gp3: encrypted, WaitForFirstConsumer, expansion allowed
Mounted at /var/uploads and /var/log/CTFd

igw.title: Internet GW
igw.body: The VPC's route to the internet. Public subnets route 0.0.0.0/0 here; NLB nodes and the NAT gateway live in those subnets.
facts: Created by terraform-aws-modules/vpc 5.0.0

nat.title: NAT GW
nat.body: single_nat_gateway = true: one NAT gateway serves the private subnets in all three AZs. Every image pull, Let's Encrypt call and S3 upload from a pod goes out through it.
facts: Losing AZ a cuts outbound traffic for every node
Cross-AZ NAT traffic is billed as data transfer
There are no VPC endpoints for ECR or S3

nlbenia.title: NLBs
nlbenia.body: Every NLB (the HTTP one and the 5 pwn ones) places a node with a public IP in each public subnet, so each AZ box holds a slice of all 6 load balancers.
facts: Subnet discovery uses the tag kubernetes.io/role/elb = 1

nlbenib.title: NLBs
nlbenib.body: Same 6 load balancers, AZ b slice.

nlbenic.title: NLBs
nlbenic.body: Same 6 load balancers, AZ c slice.

workera.title: Worker node
workera.body: EKS managed node group 'default'. Desired 3 nodes, so normally one per AZ. The scheduler decides which pods land where; this view doesn't show pod placement because it changed between deploys.
facts: Max 17 pods per node (VPC CNI limit for t3.medium)
Node role adds SSM, EBS CSI and CloudWatch agent policies
Pre-destroy state shows 4 nodes, so one AZ held two

workerc.title: Worker node
workerc.body: Same node group, AZ c. The edges from this node to the API server, ECR and S3 stand for all nodes.

ebs.title: EBS gp3 volumes
ebs.body: mariadb-data 10Gi, redis-data 1Gi, ctfd-uploads 5Gi, ctfd-logs 2Gi. Each volume exists in a single AZ. It's drawn in AZ a only as an example; the real AZ was wherever each pod first scheduled.
facts: Encrypted at rest
If that AZ fails, CTFd can't start elsewhere without restoring from the S3 backup

secrets.title: Secrets Manager
secrets.body: Holds non-IaC secrets: Docker Hub login, CTFd admin credentials, DB password, Pulumi passphrase. Terraform creates the empty secret; values are filled by migrate_secrets.py and read by secrets.py during make targets.
facts: Never written into Terraform state
make deploy-eks restores it if a teardown left it pending deletion

iam.title: IAM · IRSA
iam.body: Controllers get short-lived AWS credentials through their Kubernetes service account (IAM Roles for Service Accounts). No static keys live in the cluster.
facts: wh-2026-aws-lbc: create and manage load balancers
wh-2026-external-dns: Route 53 records
wh-2026-cert-manager: Route 53 TXT for DNS-01
wh-2026-cluster-autoscaler: change node group size
wh-2026-ctfd-backup: write to the backups bucket

cw.title: CloudWatch
cw.body: Receives node and pod metrics from the observability add-on, and holds an 8-widget ops dashboard and the alarms.
facts: Dashboard: ingress containers, node count, node CPU and memory, MariaDB memory, node filesystem, CTFd memory
Metrics and alarm history were deleted with the account

eksapi.title: EKS API
eksapi.body: The Kubernetes API server and etcd, run by AWS outside the VPC. kubelets on every node, the operator's kubectl, Terraform's Helm provider and Pulumi all talk to it.
facts: Public endpoint enabled; the creator gets cluster-admin
Add-ons: coredns, kube-proxy, vpc-cni (kept during destroy), aws-ebs-csi-driver

ecr.title: ECR
ecr.body: Private image registry. Challenge images are tagged with the challenge name in one repo; the CTFd image has its own repo.
facts: Nodes pull with the node role's ECR read permissions
wh-2026-ctfd keeps the last 5 images

s3.title: S3
s3.body: Two buckets. ctfd-backups gets the hourly database dumps. The Pulumi state bucket holds state for the ctfd, web-shared and shared-tcp stacks.
facts: Both versioned, SSE-S3 encrypted, all public access blocked
Backups expire after 30 days
The backups bucket was kept out of the final destroy

operator.title: Operator laptop
operator.sub: make in utils/ · terraform ≥1.9, pulumi, go, python3, docker, kubectl, ctfcli
operator.body: Every deploy ran from an operator's machine with AWS credentials. CI never deployed. config.ini and Secrets Manager supply the inputs.
facts: Pulumi backend: s3://wh-2026-pulumi-state; passphrase from Secrets Manager
On 2026-06-23 a local safety tool blocked make and pulumi up, so commands were run through Python subprocess instead

tf.title: Terraform
tf.body: One root module for the whole AWS foundation and the cluster add-ons. Kubernetes and Helm providers authenticate with aws eks get-token.
facts: Modules: eks ~>20.0, vpc 5.0.0, iam-role-for-service-accounts-eks
Destroy runs a cleanup script first (NLBs, security groups, ENIs)

awsres.title: AWS resources
awsres.sub: VPC, EKS, IAM, S3, ECR, SM
awsres.body: Created by the targeted first apply: the network, the cluster and node group, and the buckets and registries that later steps need.

helm.title: Helm releases
helm.body: Installed by the second apply: AWS LB Controller 3.4.0, ExternalDNS 1.21.1, ingress-nginx 4.15.1, cert-manager 1.18.2, Cluster Autoscaler 9.46.2, plus the ClusterIssuer and wildcard Certificate.

ci.title: GitHub Actions
ci.body: validate.yml runs on pull requests: challenge schema validation, terraform validate, builder unit tests and a docker functional test. It doesn't touch AWS. Only 5 of its 16 runs passed.
facts: Nothing in CI built or deployed the shared-web or shared-tcp stacks

pctfd.title: Pulumi · ctfd
pctfd.body: make deploy-ctfd: builds and pushes the CTFd image, then runs pulumi up with the secrets in stack config.
facts: Config: db_password, admin_*, secret_key, discord_webhook_url, backup_irsa_arn (all secret except the ARN)

ecrc.title: ECR wh-2026-ctfd
ecrc.body: The CTFd image repository. Deployments reference :latest, so a new push needs a pod restart to take effect.

nsctfd.title: ns ctfd
nsctfd.body: Everything the scoreboard needs, in one namespace. See the Player traffic view for the internals.

builder.title: builder.py
builder.body: The challenge pipeline. It walks every category directory, reads challenge.yml, and branches on challenge_type: shared-web, shared-tcp or static text.
facts: Fills connection_info: the URL for web, the NLB hostname for pwn
Calls ctf challenge install, then PATCHes connection_info as a safety net

docker.title: docker build
docker.body: Builds each challenge's root Dockerfile. another, loop and xoph moved to multi-stage builds in b402cc4.

ecrw.title: ECR wh-2026
ecrw.body: One repository, one tag per challenge, for example wh-2026:pokemon-portal.

pstacks.title: Pulumi stacks
pstacks.body: Two small Go programs driven by a JSON challenge list in stack config. builder.py sets that config and runs pulumi up on each.
facts: web-shared: Deployment + ClusterIP Service + Ingress
shared-tcp: Deployment + LoadBalancer Service, exports {name}-hostname

nsch.title: ns challenges-*
nsch.body: challenges-web and challenges-tcp. The NLBs for pwn challenges are created by the LB controller after the Services appear.

ctfcli.title: ctfcli
ctfcli.body: CTFd's official CLI. It reads challenge.yml (name, category, description, flags, hints, files, dynamic scoring) and creates or updates challenges through the admin API.
facts: All 39 live challenges were type dynamic, 1000 → 100 over 31 solves
2 pwn challenges ended up linear with decay 1; the cause is unknown

ctfdapi.title: CTFd API
ctfdapi.body: The same CTFd pod, reached over HTTPS with the preset admin token. Both ctfcli and builder.py write here.

cia.title: CW agents
cia.body: EKS add-on amazon-cloudwatch-observability, installed by Terraform. Runs a DaemonSet on every node.
facts: Worker role has CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy

alarms.title: 5 alarms
alarms.body: ingress-nginx pod down, node count below minimum, MariaDB memory > 80%, node filesystem > 85%, node memory > 85%.
facts: state_value was None in the pre-destroy state; whether any fired is unknown

sns.title: SNS topic
sns.body: Fans alarms out to email subscribers and to the Discord relay Lambda.

email.title: Email
email.body: Each address must confirm the SNS subscription before it receives anything.

lambda.title: Lambda
lambda.body: A small function (zip in utils/eks/lambda/) that turns the SNS alarm JSON into a Discord message.

discord.title: Discord
discord.body: Receives three kinds of message: CloudWatch alarms via Lambda, healthcheck failures, and CTFd first-blood announcements.

backup.title: Backup CronJob
backup.body: Hourly mysqldump of the CTFd database, gzipped and copied to S3 by an aws-cli container. Runs as service account ctfd-backup (IRSA).
facts: Keeps the last 3 successful and 3 failed jobs
make backup-ctfd and make restore-ctfd do the same by hand

s3b.title: S3 ctfd-backups
s3b.body: Versioned bucket for the hourly dumps. It was deliberately kept when the rest of the account was destroyed.
facts: One verified artifact: ctfd-20260628-120001.sql

health.title: Healthcheck
health.body: python:3.12-alpine running healthcheck.py: HTTP check per web challenge, TCP connect per pwn challenge, and a heartbeat summary.
facts: Keeps 2 successful and 5 failed jobs
NLB hostnames are configured in the CronJob env, so they go stale if the stack is recreated

endpoints.title: Endpoints
endpoints.body: The same public endpoints players use, probed from inside the cluster. A pass means 'answers', not 'solvable': pokemon-portal passed and still had 0 solves.

certm.title: cert-manager
certm.body: Issues and renews every certificate in the cluster: ctfd-tls, one {name}-tls per web challenge, and the wildcard-challenges default certificate for *.whitehats-ctf.com.
facts: ClusterIssuer and Certificate are applied by kubectl inside Terraform null_resources
A wildcard covers one label only, so *.whitehats-ctf.com doesn't cover x.challenges.whitehats-ctf.com; per-Ingress certificates do that job

le.title: Let's Encrypt
le.body: The public CA that signs the certificates. Production endpoint, with rate limits: 5 duplicate certificates per week per name set.

extdns.title: ExternalDNS
extdns.body: Keeps Route 53 in step with the cluster. Restricted to the whitehats-ctf.com domain and tagged with owner id wh-2026-eks, so it only deletes records it created.

ca.title: Autoscaler
ca.body: Watches for unschedulable pods and resizes the node group. Scale-down: node under 50% requested for 10 min, no sooner than 10 min after a scale-up. New nodes get 5 min to join.
facts: skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false, skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false

asg.title: EC2 Auto Scaling
asg.body: The Auto Scaling group behind the EKS managed node group. Desired size started at 3 and was 4 in the pre-destroy state; scaling history is gone.
